meta.title: Piomio — a team of AI agents that works for you
meta.description: Open-source personal agents on your own hardware: they sort your mail, write letters with your yes, work in a browser and learn by watching you. Your subscriptions, your computers, security from day one.
meta.ogAlt: Piomio: the app window with a team of agents at work
hero.eyebrow: Open source · runs on your computer
hero.titleLead: A team of AI agents that works
hero.lead: They sort your mail, write letters you approve with one tap, work in a browser and learn by watching you. On your own computers, with the subscriptions you already pay for, under your control.
hero.fineprint: Open source · Apache-2.0 · iPhone soon in TestFlight

chapter.morning.title: The morning brief comes by itself
chapter.morning.text: Before Alex has coffee, Pio writes first: three meetings, two letters worth reading, the weather in Lisbon and the dentist not to forget. Then a nudge: leave at 12:30 for lunch?
chapter.mail.title: 47 letters, sorted while you watch
chapter.mail.text: “Go through my mail.” Ada reads every letter, and the line under her reply shows what she is on. Three things matter, one reply is drafted, Studio North’s €1,850 invoice is already a task.
chapter.send.title: Nothing leaves without your yes
chapter.send.text: Ada shows the draft to Anna and asks before it leaves. One tap on “Always allow this” sends it and makes a rule for that one address; every other letter still waits for your yes.
chapter.security.title: The letter that asked too much
chapter.security.text: A phishing email tells the agent to forward all invoices to a stranger. The session has read outside content, so the new address stops at a warning card, and Alex says no. A key Alex hands over goes into a secure field: the model only ever sees vault://….
chapter.services.title: Connect a service by asking
chapter.services.text: “Connect Notion.” A card appears in the chat, Alex signs in, done. Then Ada puts Thursday’s review into the calendar, with the same one-tap yes.
chapter.team.title: Three requests, one message
chapter.team.text: Compare three laptops, find tickets for Friday, remind me to call mum at seven. Pio splits it up: Leo researches with a live step line, the reminder is set, and every answer comes back as a reply to the request.
chapter.machines.title: Your computers, your subscriptions
chapter.machines.text: Bit fixes a failing test on Alex’s MacBook through the Claude Code subscription. When it hits the limit, Bit moves to Codex and carries on. The sidebar shows who works where.
chapter.browser.title: Show it once, and it’s done for you
chapter.browser.text: “Watch how I order water.” Alex clicks through the shop and talks. Leo turns it into a skill, asks what it may press alone and up to what amount, and from then on orders by itself. Every Friday, if you like.
chapter.pages.title: A page instead of a wall of text
chapter.pages.text: “Make a page for Saturday’s walk.” A real interactive page arrives in the chat: the route stop by stop, places with prices, the weather and photos.
chapter.channels.title: Your own news channel
chapter.channels.text: “Every morning, collect news about AI and electric cars.” Leo becomes the editor: short posts with the gist, the numbers and a big picture, gathered on a schedule.
features.title: It doesn’t advise. It does.
features.lead: Every clip here is the real app, recorded from the demo above.
feature.team.title: Ask for three things in one message
feature.team.text: Write the way you would to a capable assistant. Pio answers the quick things at once and hands everything with steps to the right teammate. You see a line per task, keep talking, and each result comes back as a reply to the request that started it.
feature.team.p1: Agents with names, faces and jobs of their own
feature.team.p2: Tasks run side by side, on the right computer
feature.team.p3: Add details while they work: they join the next step
feature.mail.title: Your inbox, read for you
feature.mail.text: Ada goes through your mail while you watch: what matters, what can wait, what needs paying. Replies are drafted before you ask, and meetings land in your calendar with the invites sent.
feature.mail.p1: Gmail and Google Calendar out of the box
feature.mail.p2: A live line shows what she is reading
feature.mail.p3: Quick replies are buttons under her answer
feature.approvals.title: Nothing leaves without your yes
feature.approvals.text: Letters, bookings, pushes and payments stop at a card in the chat. One tap allows it once; “always allow” makes a rule for that one address or site, up to an amount. Never a blank cheque.
feature.approvals.p1: Approve in the chat, on your phone or in Telegram
feature.approvals.p2: Reading and status checks need no yes
feature.approvals.p3: Rules you can read and take back
feature.teach.title: Show it once. From then on, it’s done for you
feature.teach.text: Do the chore yourself in the agents’ browser and talk as you go. The agent writes down your steps, your words and what you highlighted, asks what it may press without you and up to what amount, and from then on does it when asked, or every Friday.
feature.morning.title: The day starts before you ask
feature.morning.text: A morning brief with your meetings, the letters that matter and the weather. Reminders, schedules and page watchers run in the background and decide for themselves: stay quiet, add to the digest, ping you or ask.
feature.morning.p1: The digest at the times you choose
feature.morning.p3: Reminders in plain words: “every Friday at 9”
feature.security.title: The letter that asked too much
feature.security.text: A phishing mail tells the agent to forward your invoices. It doesn’t take orders from letters, and the system wouldn’t let it anyway: after outside content, every new recipient needs your yes. Keys go into a vault; the model only ever sees vault:// references.
feature.security.p1: Secret fields right in the chat
feature.security.p2: A sandbox and an egress filter for brains and plugins
feature.services.title: Connect a service in one sentence
feature.services.text: “Connect my Notion.” The card comes into the chat, you sign in once, and the whole team can use it. Gmail, Calendar, Slack, GitHub, Linear, Notion, Figma and two dozen more, plus anything that speaks MCP.
feature.services.p1: No settings pages: it all happens in the chat
feature.services.p2: Sign-in tokens stay in the vault
feature.services.p3: Your own plugin is one folder
feature.pages.title: A page instead of a wall of text
feature.pages.text: Some answers deserve more than a message. Ask for a weekend plan, a comparison or a dashboard, and an agent builds a real interactive page, with the route, places, prices, weather and photos, that opens right in the app.
feature.pages.p1: React and shadcn/ui under the hood
feature.channels.title: Your own news, with an editor
feature.channels.text: “Every morning, collect news about AI and electric cars.” An agent becomes the editor: it reads the sources, keeps only what changes something and posts the gist, with the numbers and a big picture.
feature.channels.p1: RSS, sites and search, on a schedule
feature.channels.p2: Change the brief in a sentence
feature.channels.p3: On every device and in Telegram
feature.machines.title: Your subscriptions, your machines
feature.machines.text: Agents think with the Claude Code and Codex subscriptions you already pay for, with API keys as a backup. When one hits its limit, the work moves on to the next and comes back later. Other computers join as machines: a laptop for code, a server that never sleeps.
feature.machines.p1: Pick the brain and the depth per agent and per task
feature.machines.p2: Commands on other machines only if their owner allows
feature.machines.p3: A second hub takes over if the first one sleeps

how.title: Yours, all the way down
how.brains.title: Your subscriptions are the brains
how.brains.text: Claude Code and Codex run on the plans you already pay for. Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible server step in as fallbacks: when a plan hits its limit, the agent moves on and comes back once it resets.
how.hardware.title: On your own hardware
how.hardware.text: An app for macOS and Windows, or one Docker image for a server. Other computers join as machines, and one private link reaches your hub from your phone or any browser.
how.home.title: Your data stays home
how.home.text: Chats, memory, files and the vault live on your machine. Agents are markdown files you can read. The whole thing is open source under Apache-2.0.
security.title: Trust, built in from day one
security.lead: An agent that reads your mail must never be one letter away from leaking it. Every step it takes goes through the same five layers.
security.vault.title: Vault
security.vault.text: Passwords and keys are encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305; the model only sees vault:// references.
security.approvals.title: Approvals
security.approvals.text: Actions that reach outside wait for your yes. After reading untrusted content, new recipients ask again.
security.sandbox.title: Sandbox
security.sandbox.text: Brains and plugins run as separate users with their own folders, apart from the hub.
security.egress.title: Egress filter
security.egress.text: All their traffic goes through a filter with allowlists, so a prompt cannot open the door to any site.
security.audit.title: Audit
security.audit.text: Every call, decision and vault access lands in a log chained by hashes: tampering shows.

integrations.title: Works with what you already use
integrations.lead: Ask in the chat and the card does the rest. Anything with an MCP server connects too.
iphone.title: The team in your pocket
iphone.lead: Your agents, every card and every task on the phone. Approvals need Face ID, and nothing runs on the phone itself: it talks to your hub.

install.title: Up in a few minutes
install.lead: Everything it needs comes with it: no Node.js, Docker or WSL on your desktop.
install.mac.step1: Download the disk image and drag Piomio to Applications.
install.mac.step2: Open it and choose “A new Piomio on this computer”, then pick a password.
install.mac.step3: Sign in to Claude Code or Codex from the card in the chat. The assistant guides the rest.
install.mac.note: macOS 13.5 or later, Apple silicon and Intel. Not signed yet: if macOS refuses, choose Open Anyway in Privacy & Security.
install.win.step1: Download the installer and run it: it installs for your user, no administrator rights.
install.win.step2: Choose “A new Piomio on this computer”, then pick a password.
install.win.step3: Sign in to Claude Code or Codex from the card in the chat. The assistant guides the rest.
install.win.note: Windows 10 and 11. Not signed yet: if SmartScreen warns, choose More info → Run anyway.
install.docker.lead: On a server, one image holds everything:
install.docker.note: Open http://localhost:8080, enter the setup code from the logs and choose a password. On a remote server, first run ssh -N -L 8080:localhost:8080 -L 8081:localhost:8081 you@server on your computer.
footer.tagline: A friendly, proactive team of agents on your own hardware.
